glosses: to upset, wreck
to unsettle

examples.text: Rien ne détraque autant un esprit qu'une pareille instruction, faite à bâtons rompus, ne reposant sur aucune base solide. Le plus souvent, ces miettes de science donnent une idée absolument fausse des hautes vérités, et rendent les pauvres d'esprit insupportables de carrure bête.
examples.translation: Nothing so derails a mind as like instruction, offered haphazardly, resting on no solid basis. More often than not, these crumbs of knowledge give an absolutely false impression of noble truths and renders the weak-witted unbearably, unshakably stupid.
examples.english: Nothing so derails a mind as like instruction, offered haphazardly, resting on no solid basis. More often than not, these crumbs of knowledge give an absolutely false impression of noble truths and renders the weak-witted unbearably, unshakably stupid.

glosses: Faire perdre à un cheval ses bonnes allures, son allure ordinaire.

examples.text: Celui qui a monté ce cheval l’a tout détraqué.

glosses: Déranger dans ses fonctions une machine, une chose organisée jusqu’à la mettre hors d’état de fonctionner.

examples.text: On répandit l'idée que les Roms n'étaient qu'un ramassis de feignants dont la feignantise détraquait le bon fonctionnement du monde libre.

glosses: Déranger un organe dans ses fonctions, un être intelligent dans ses facultés.

examples.text: Ce médicament lui a détraqué l’estomac.
— Ce jeune homme savait tout, mon cher monsieur ! dit-il en posant sur une table le volume où sont contenues les œuvres de Spinosa. Comment une tête si bien organisée a-t-elle pu se détraquer ?
Quelques témoignages recueillis après l’extermination du vampire et les détails qu’on put deviner sont à détraquer l’entendement.

glosses: Perdre sa régularité dans son fonctionnement.

examples.text: L’année d’auparavant, sa moissonneuse mécanique s’était détraquée ; et, désespéré du mauvais vouloir de ses serviteurs, arrivant à douter lui-même de l’efficacité des machines, il avait dû se précautionner d’une équipe de moissonneurs, dès l’Ascension.
Et dans ce rire acharné, grandissant, dans ce rire pareil à un réveille-matin qui se détraque, j’entendis ces mots, coupés de roulades sonores et de fusées sifflantes […]

translations.source_sense_description: (En particulier) (Équitation) Faire perdre à un cheval ses bonnes allures, son allure ordinaire.

glosses: Causar destrucción y ruina.

examples.text: El terremoto de Chillán en 1939 arruinó la ciudad que hubo que reconstruir en otro emplazamiento, y ostenta el triste récord de víctimas fatales en la historia de los terremotos de Chile: 24.000.
De aquí que cuando en 1846 se produjo una plaga que arruinó la cosecha de patata, la mayor parte de la población rural se quedo sin alimentos.

glosses: Causar un desastre económico a personas, empresas o países.
tags: se usa también como verbo pronominal

examples.text: La bajada masiva del valor de las acciones arruinó a muchísimos inversores, cerró empresas y bancos, condenó al paro a millones de personas y, debido al efecto dominó, trasladó el mismo problema a muchas naciones.
Como resultado de la crisis económica subsecuente, un amplio segmento de la clase media se arruinó, el comercio fue monopolizado por judios alemanes.

glosses: Causarle un daño muy grande a algo material o inmaterial.

examples.text: Aquella excursión le arruinó y fue el factor desencadenante que contribuyó también a arruinar su salud.

glosses: Dicho de una persona, causarle un grave daño moral.

translations.source_sense_description: (Par analogie) Déranger dans ses fonctions une machine, une chose organisée jusqu’à la mettre hors d’état de fonctionner.

glosses: To throw into confusion or disorder.

examples.text: Hecklers disrupted the man's speech.

glosses: To interrupt or impede.

examples.text: Work on the tunnel was disrupted by a strike.
The Glaswegians bore good-humouredly the mishaps which occasionally disrupted the services during the first month.

Irregular bedtimes may disrupt healthy brain development in young children, according to a study of intelligence and sleeping habits. ¶ Going to bed at a different time each night affected girls more than boys, but both fared worse on mental tasks than children who had a set bedtime, researchers found.
In the Canadian and Alaskan Arctic region, where 2°C warming has already occurred since 1950, the loss of coastal sea ice and permafrost is disrupting traditional Inuit hunting routines.

The scientific instruments of the day recorded rapid fluctuations in the Earth's magnetic field, as powerful electrical currents flowed through the upper atmosphere. Ships' logs noted observations of the northern lights as far south as the Caribbean, and telegraph systems across the world were disrupted as electrical currents were induced in the copper lines.

glosses: To improve a product or service in ways that displace an established one and surprise the market.

examples.text: The internet makes it easier for leaner businesses to disrupt the larger and more unwieldy ones.

glosses: Torn off or torn asunder; severed; disrupted.

glosses: To stop functioning.

examples.text: I am afraid my computer will break down if I try to run it at too high a speed.

glosses: To unexpectedly collapse, physically or in structure.
To intentionally demolish; to pull down.
To fail, especially socially or for political reasons.

examples.text: Talks broke down between Prime Minister John Doe and the opposition party.
Relations broke down between Greece and Turkey.

glosses: To give in or give up: relent, concede, surrender.

examples.text: Is it worth taking it to a repair shop, or should I just break down and buy a new one?

glosses: To render or to become unstable due to stress, to collapse physically or mentally.

examples.text: Near-synonym: come undone
She is back to work now, after she broke down the other day.
Sophia broke down here. Even at this moment she was subconsciously comparing her rendering of the part of the forlorn bride with Miss Marie Lohr's.
As to Ernest... He is quite as nervously broken down as I am but it manifests itself in different ways. His inclination is towards megalomania and mine towards melancholy.

glosses: To render or to become weak and ineffective.

examples.text: Hodgson's approach may not illuminate proceedings in Poland and Ukraine but early evidence suggests they will be tough to break down.
His authority and influence over his coordinates broke down gradually.

glosses: To (cause to) decay, to decompose.

examples.text: Leaves and grass will break down into compost faster if you keep them moist.

glosses: To separate into a number of parts.

examples.text: Near-synonyms: break apart, break up, take apart, tear down, tear up
The goods station is a transhipment centre (centre de transbordement) at which loads made up at other centres are broken down and redespatched to destinations in the area.
Meetings began in June and shortly after the group of twelve women decided to break-down into two sub groups in order to examine the subject more efficiently.

glosses: To divide into parts to give more details, to provide a more indepth analysis of.

examples.text: Near-synonym: analyze
If you don't understand, ask him to break down the numbers for you.

glosses: To digest.

examples.text: Near-synonym: catabolize
His stomach took a while to break down his food.
His food took a while to break down in his stomach.

glosses: Misspelling of breakdown.

glosses: To worsen; to fail or go amiss; to have a bad outcome.

examples.text: Everything seems to be going very badly wrong today.
If you want good weather, you can't go wrong with Spain.
I just don't know what went wrong!

Johnson explained that absolute gauging assumed that everything that could go wrong would go wrong at the same time, resulting in the train hitting the platform. In contrast, probabilistic gauging says that everything can go wrong, but not at the same time.

glosses: To malfunction.

examples.text: The vending machine went wrong and dispensed five cans of drink at once.

glosses: To become wicked or depraved.

examples.text: Mr. Blue Sky / Please tell us why / You had to hide away for so long (so long) / Where did we go wrong?
